files.notes: The hole sewing pair was made by the SVG import, not by Modify Overlap > Set hole sewing: after import, Modify Overlap showed Cancel hole sewing enabled for the pentagon. Cancelling it and then selecting both shapes and choosing Set hole sewing reported 'Invalid pair was selected!!' every time (also with Ctrl+A), so the import's own pair was kept. The import centres the pentagon and star on the page: the pentagon shows 38.00 x 36.20 mm (spec 38.04 x 36.18 mm), about 1.7 mm lower than the spec's absolute position; the star keeps its place relative to the pentagon. Thread colours mapped by the import were not changed.

files.settings: File > New, Design Page Custom Size 100 x 100 mm; grid 1 mm, Snap to Grid on; Rectangle tool: line Not Sewn (Line), region Fill Stitch with Under sewing unticked and every other attribute at its default (density 4.5 line/mm, Manual straight line 45 degrees, step pitch 4.0 mm, frequency 30 %, pull compensation 0.0 mm), colour BROTHER EMBROIDERY 800 RED; three 10 x 10 mm squares drawn with top-left corners at (0,0), (50,0), (25,0) mm in that order; Optimize Sewing Order clicked (Sewing Order pane); Save As PES (default type: Layout & Editing Ver.11.0 File, header #PES0110)
files.notes: Option > Options > Optimize Entry/Exit Points was ON (default here, not changed). 182 stitches per square. The squares sew in drawing order (x 0, 50, 25); the exit of each square and the entry of the next are on the facing corners (jumps 40.0 and 15.0 mm). Black-box tests of the command (gui-optimize-findings in the track notes): with or without the option, Optimize Sewing Order keeps drawing order within a colour, groups colours (red 0, blue 50, red 25 became red 0, red 25, blue 50), and links entry/exit only between same-colour neighbours. Round 1 (PR #34) made the same design with under sewing on: same order, gaps 41.3 and 16.3 mm, because the under sewing starts 1 mm inside the outline.
